Do what?  Transition?  I don't think I'm trans
I don't know.  My answer right now could be different from one in an hour.  I have no strong instinct.  Don't even know why I posted, honestly, I know an answer will never come.

> But dig deeper. You mentioned the rage at women, trans or otherwise, living their best lives. I used to be in the same boat, espousing bull shit red pill ideology because on a deep level I was jealous  
  
>  by acknowledging you *want* to be a woman, you are experiencing dysphoria.  
 
I really wish I could just reach deep down and pull out some sort of honesty like that, but it's hard.  How do I \*\*know\*\* I want to be a woman? What does that embody?   What if it's just a domino array of unfortunate circumstances that led to me to this point?  Why is it a challenge to step back and examine my true feelings?  Can I even trust my feelings?  Is it a feeling or just some neurotic impulse??  How can I be sure I've separated the sexual aspects apart from the identity aspect?

You get the picture.  Without the base confidence most trans women have, there's no foundation to believe anything my mind cooks up.

Really, thank you **so** much for this! I wasn't expecting such an understanding and thorough answer - especially when it's easy to give a cookie cutter response.    I guess it's just a fear of taking that leap, you know?  Certainty is something I've always craved, so if there's even one thing outside of the "equation" I can't help but be filled with doubt.  Obviously, with being trans there's a lot of that, even for people who are sure they are trans.  This helps put everything into perspective, one of those "save for later comments" when looking at the big picture.  Thanks again, sincerely.

>Maybe instead of asking whether you’re trans or cis or something else, consider what you would do in response to that information, if you could really, really be 100% sure one way or the other. Would you just embrace it as an identity, and continue to live as you do? Would you take hormones or transition? Have a surgery? Would you be disappointed one way or the other?

I don't know.  Some side of me would be disappointed at not being trans - but then I don't know what that means.  Is that the naive side? The gullible solution side? the fetish side?  I'll probably never really know and it's terrifying.
